status: Frozen before first numerical execution; no outcome-dependent tuning
purpose: Test technical increment against standard sign-aware convex secant bounds on exactly matched observations
cases: All 256 parent cases, both horizons, both targets; retain calibration failures

methods.current_symmetric: Reuse frozen 145-cell symmetric-curvature intervals; replay first four seeds of each truth at horizon 16
methods.classical_sign_convex: Same 145 cells, 291 nonnegative weights, loading, noise bands and solver; positive-segment convex secants give only downward remainder and negative segments only upward remainder
methods.finite_grid_diagnostic: Same parent 289 positive rates plus equilibrium, no interpolation error; narrower finite-spectrum model, not a continuum-valid competitor

gate.definition: At horizon 16, current symmetric method must reduce BOTH target mean widths by >=10% versus classical_sign_convex for >=2 truth groups including one continuous family, while both continuum methods cover all valid-calibration cases
gate.interpretation: Engineering increment screen, not novelty proof; domination by an elementary convex bound closes the present solver-superiority claim

reference.location: Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization (2004), Section 3.1.1
reference.scope: Convex function lies below its endpoint chord. Our implementation combines this established fact with the already used interpolation remainder; not a replication of a named relaxation-spectrum software package.

limitations: Synthetic matched post-observation interval comparison; no external material experiment
No new loading, noise, seed, mesh, target or truth selection
